findings.what: The commit discharge arcs read as outlined neon zigzags rather than lightning: each bolt is 6-10 long straight segments with large acute corners, and every branch stops dead at full stroke width with a round cap in mid-air. findings.evidence: scratchpad/arc-left.png (my seated frame, 3x, src x110-360 y1240-1540) vs scratchpad/arc-ref.png (reference 03, same scale): the build's left group has two prongs above the collar ending blunt in open space and a lasso-like closed loop around the collar; roughly 8 kinks per run. Cause is visible in source: src/fx/arcPaths.ts buildBolt uses segments = clamp(len/9, 8..24) with amp = min(len*0.09,10)*chaos, and Lever.tsx passes chaos 1.8-2.1, so the displacement amplitude is roughly one segment length; src/fx/Arc.tsx strokes every path and every branch at a constant strokeWidth with strokeLinecap='round', so nothing tapers. Core/halo widths themselves are fine (build core 8 device px at y=1490 vs reference 10 at y=1446).
findings.fix: In src/fx: raise the segment count (or cut amp) so kink frequency is 3-4x the displacement amplitude, and taper branches to zero width at their free end — either per-segment strokes with decreasing width or a tapered polygon — so an offshoot fades out instead of stopping at full width. Leave the main bolt's endpoints on the rails as they are.
